A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Early Cutting research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison despite extensive reformatting. Ambiguities in some new experimental descriptions are identifiable within v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original learning-order experiments, feature-space analyses, and Early Cutting evaluations in Sections 2–4 and Tables 1–6.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and reports additional runtime, ablation, and transfer experiments in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The original filtering criteria and three-round procedure remain unchanged. Appendix B.8 adds Early Cutting (Faster), a limited procedural variant performing one sample-selection iteration instead of three.

E1.justification: Table 10 adds Fashion-MNIST evaluation with 40% instance-dependent label noise. Existing CIFAR, CIFAR-N, WebVision/ILSVRC12, and full ImageNet-1k coverage is retained, making this a limited extension within noisy-label classification.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 add VOG (Agarwal et al., 2022) and Misdetect (Deng et al., 2024) to both CIFAR comparisons. Table 5 removes CSGN's reported full-ImageNet result while retaining its WebVision and ILSVRC12 results. Most comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce Tiny-ViT on CIFAR-10 and a one-versus-three-selection-round comparison. Existing splits, training settings, and metrics are retained. The new ablation's exact dataset and procedure remain unresolved, and Table 8's symmetric-noise caption conflicts with values appearing under instance-dependent noise in Table 3.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained learning-order diagnostics and threshold sensitivity analysis, v2 adds component-removal ablations (Table 9), a runtime–accuracy tradeoff analysis (Table 8), and fixed-parameter transfer checks (Table 10). These substantially expand the analytical questions examined, although Appendix B.9 leaves the ablation setting and early-cutting-rate removal insufficiently specified.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean±std in the CIFAR comparisons and dispersion in learning curves. New rows follow existing reporting practices; v2 supplies no new independent-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: The results expand substantially through added baseline scores and appendix experiments, including 69.53±0.10% for the faster variant, 84.57% versus 83.12% in the ablation, and 75.42%/94.11% for Tiny-ViT/Fashion-MNIST. Table 5 replaces CSGN's 40.68% ImageNet result with a dash. Retained Early Cutting scores in Tables 1–6 are unchanged; ambiguous new settings limit direct performance comparisons.

T1.justification: Appendix B.8 adds an asymptotic cost derivation: metric computation and filtering take O(n), sorting takes O(n log n), and the filtering application therefore costs O(n log n). Existing mathematical definitions and Equations 1–13 remain equivalent apart from notation.

C1.justification: The central claims about MEEs' disproportionate harm, their feature-space characteristics, and removal through later-model recalibration remain intact. The abstract and conclusion retain their meaning; merging the introduction's contribution bullets does not change their substance.

C2.justification: New appendix discussion interprets component importance, computational tradeoffs, and transferability. Conversely, v2 removes v1's Impact Statement, including specific cautions that learning-dynamics assumptions may fail across architectures or distributions and that discarding valuable difficult examples could introduce bias or reduce fairness.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the analyzed feature representation as preceding the final fully connected layer and adds runtime breakdowns, including per-epoch and cumulative filtering timings. The fixed 10%/20%/20% filtering proportions were already documented in v1 Appendix B.5; their inclusion in Section 3 is not a new implementation setting.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Agarwal et al. (2022), Deng et al. (2024), and Wang et al. (2022), while removing Pleiss et al. (2020) and associated example-consistency discussion. The broader positioning around misleading early-learning confidence remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 expands the title, merges contribution bullets, makes Related Work an unnumbered heading, revises parts of Section 3, and distinguishes learning-time notation from loss notation. It also removes the Impact Statement and reorganizes Appendix B, while retaining most existing prose and the main section sequence.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to a single column, with substantially different margins, scaling, and figure/table placement. v1's runtime Table 7 becomes the restructured v2 Table 8, alongside new Tables 7, 9, and 10. Figure 3 receives revised, visibly overlapping vertical-axis labels.

improvement.justification: Added baselines, transfer experiments, and computational analysis broaden the evidence. However, Table 8 labels values matching Table 3's instance-noise column as symmetric-noise results, while Appendix B.9 leaves its dataset, noise setting, and one ablation definition unresolved. v2 also removes specific limitations stated in v1. These benefits and reporting weaknesses prevent a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
